topIssues.title: [PCD] Add starting anchor root and prestate hashes to the deploy input
topIssues.author: 0xOneTony
topIssues.body: OPCM's `FullConfig` struct on the contracts side already accepts a `startingAnchorRoot` and per-game-type prestate hashes in `disputeGameConfigs[]`. The Go-side `DeployOPChainInput` struct that `op-deployer` populates does not yet expose those fields — it carries a single `DisputeAbsolutePrestate` constant and no anchor root. Extend the Go struct with the new fields, populate them from state in the stage that builds the deploy input, and wire them through both execution paths.

topPRs.title: op-reth: forward eth_getBlockReceipts to historical endpoint
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Sebastian Stammler** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784709825702899)_

**Before:** `eth_getBlockReceipts` and several other block-parameterized read methods (`eth_getHeaderByNumber`/`ByHash`, `eth_getBlockTransactionCountByNumber`/`ByHash`, `eth_getUncleCountByBlockNumber`/`ByBlockHash`, `eth_getUncleByBlockNumberAndIndex`/`ByBlockHashAndIndex`, `eth_getTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex`/`ByBlockHashAndIndex`, `eth_getRawTransactionByBlockNumberAndIndex`/`ByBlockHashAndIndex`) for pre-bedrock blocks were served locally by op-reth, which has no pre-bedrock data, instead of being forwarded to the configured historical RPC endpoint like the other block-based methods.

**After:** `eth_getBlockReceipts` and all of the above block-parameterized methods for a pre-bedrock block are forwarded to the historical endpoint, matching `eth_getBlockByNumber`/`eth_getBlockByHash` and the rest of the forwarded set.

Since plain l2geth does not implement `eth_getBlockReceipts`, the middleware additionally stitches the response when the forwarded call comes back with JSON-RPC error `-32601` (method not found): it fetches the block from the historical endpoint with transaction hashes only (`full=false`) and issues one `eth_getTransactionReceipt` per hash (pre-bedrock OP Mainnet blocks contain exactly one transaction), returning the legacy receipt objects verbatim — self-consistent with what the forwarded `eth_getTransactionReceipt` already returns. Historical endpoints that serve `eth_getBlockReceipts` natively (op-erigon, routing proxies) keep the single-call forward path.

Edge cases: a block unknown to the historical endpoint returns `null` (mirroring a node that serves the method natively), a block without transactions returns `[]`, and any failure while stitching returns a JSON-RPC error to the caller instead of falling through to local handling (which cannot serve pre-bedrock receipts). All other forwarded methods keep the existing behavior exactly.

**How:** In `rust/op-reth/crates/rpc/src/historical.rs`: added the methods to the position-0 block-id arm of `extract_block_id_for_method`, and added a `-32601`-triggered stitch path (`stitch_block_receipts` / `fetch_stitched_block_receipts`) to `HistoricalRpcInner::forward_to_historical`. Unit tests cover block-id extraction plus mocked-transport tests for the native forward path, the stitch path (number and hash params), empty block, unknown block, receipt-failure error, and fall-through preservation for other methods.

Fixes #21031

---

topPRs.title: op-devstack: Wait for the destination chain before sending executing messages
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
An executing message whose block predates the initiating message it references is invalid, so consolidation replaces the block. Nothing waited for the destination chain to catch up before submitting the exec tx, so whenever it lagged the source chain the test got a replaced block.

That is what failed `TestInteropFaultProofs_DepositMessage/SP1NativeCore` on [pipeline 131101](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/131101/workflows/e0ef036d-80b8-44fc-b399-9faa9abbbd17/jobs/5377289): chain B sequenced the exec message into a block at ts 1785190016 while the init log on chain A was at ts 1785190020, and the supernode invalidated it — `initiating timestamp 1785190020 > executing timestamp 1785190016` — leaving one optimistic root replaced where the checkpoint expected none.

Every path that submits an executing message now waits for the destination chain to build past the initiating timestamp:

- `EOA.SendExecMessage`, `SendInvalidExecMessage`, `SendPackedExecMessages`, `PrepareExecTx`
- `EOA.WaitForInitMessages` is exported for the tests that build exec txs with `txintent` directly (`interop/message`, `interop/reorgs`)
- `interopsmoke` hits the same race against live chains, so `remoteUser` waits too

The wait is strict (`initTs + 1`), matching the interop load test, which already did this inline: op-geth filters pending executing messages against the unsafe head timestamp rather than the pending block ([op-geth#603](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/603)).

Not changed: `SameTimestampPair.SubmitExecTo` / `SubmitExecForMessage`. Those reference precomputed identifiers for blocks the test sequencer has not built yet, so there is nothing to wait for.

## Test plan

All with a local `op-reth`:

- `./tests/interop/message/` — full package, PASS (180s). Covers all six raw `txintent` sites plus `TestRandomDirectedGraph` via `SendPackedExecMessages`.
- `./tests/interop/reorgs/ -run TestReorgInitExecMsg` — PASS (45s).
- `./tests/supernode/interop/ -run TestSupernodeInteropBidirectionalMessages` — PASS (33s).

The guard was confirmed to act on real values, not to be a no-op: instrumented, `TestInitExecMsg` logged `initTs=1785192212 headTs=1785192214`; with the target temporarily forced to `initTs + 20`, the wait blocked until the chain reached it (head `initTs+20`, runtime 17.7s -> 35.9s) and the test still passed.

topPRs.title: op-reth: make forwarded txpool admission opt-in (breaking)
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Makes local transaction-pool admission opt-in for RPC-submitted transactions that are forwarded to a configured sequencer.

- Adds `--rollup.txpool.enable-admission`, disabled by default and without aliases.
- When forwarding is configured, transactions are retained locally only when admission is enabled.
- Nodes without a configured sequencer continue to admit submitted transactions normally.
- Adds a Rust node integration test using a mock sequencer to cover both modes.

## Breaking change

Forwarding op-reth nodes currently retain forwarded transactions in their local pool by default. After this change, they will not.

This affects local transaction-pool RPC responses and pending nonce calculation. Operators that rely on the existing behavior must explicitly set `--rollup.txpool.enable-admission`.

| Sequencer configured | Admission enabled | Transaction retained locally |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No | Either | Yes |
| Yes | No (default) | No |
| Yes | Yes | Yes |

## Motivation

A forwarding node does not build blocks, so its local pool can otherwise expose transactions that it merely relayed and may not reflect the sequencer's pending state. Making admission opt-in aligns the default behavior with op-geth.

## Credit

This PR supersedes #21665, originally authored by @asdv23. The core implementation and rationale are theirs, and their original commit authorship is preserved. This PR carries that work forward with the canonical flag spelling, integration coverage, and concise documentation.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-node --lib args`
- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-node --test it`
- `cargo clippy -p reth-optimism-node --tests -- -D warnings`

Fixes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/124

topPRs.title: op-supernode: Rewind interop accepted state when L2 safe head reorgs
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
## What

Adds an L2 frontier canonicality guard to the interop verifier's decision loop. When the last verified L2 head is no longer canonical on a chain, `observeRound` now emits `DecisionRewind` instead of `DecisionAdvance`.

## Why

During the Reorg-4 rehearsal, working supernodes wedged forever retrying an impossible `persistFrontierLogs` append with `ErrParentHashMismatch`:

```
persist frontier logs: chain 420120178: block 191137 parent hash 0x56b58e… does not match logsDB last sealed block hash 0x755661…
```

Reaching that error inside `DecisionAdvance` is an invariant violation, not a recoverable round error. `DecisionAdvance` assumes the previous frontier is verified and canonical and appends its child; a parent mismatch means the decision was made against a fork the sealed logsDB tip is not on.

Root cause: the interop verifier is the sole authority for its own safe head, so the canonical block at the last verified height should always equal the verified head. It stopped matching because the verifier's EL was driven off the safe chain by a non-safe-descendant sequencer gossip payload it adopted without rolling back (a separate EL/CL-layer defect). Once canonical `191136` changed underneath the accepted frontier, the decision loop kept choosing `DecisionAdvance` toward the new-fork `191137` because `observeRound` only guarded **L1** inclusion canonicality — it never re-checked that the last verified **L2** frontier was still canonical.

The repair machinery already exists (`buildRewindPlan` / `applyRewindPlan` for `DecisionRewind`, wired to rewind verifiedDB + logsDB to the previous verified head); it was simply never reached for an L2-only reorg. This PR closes that gap: detect the stale frontier and route into the existing rewind path, which walks the accepted frontier back one timestamp per round until it reconverges on the canonical common ancestor, after which normal advance re-seals the replacement branch.

This is defense-in-depth. The underlying invariant break — a verifier's safe head being reorgable by gossip — must be fixed at the EL/CL layer; absent that bug the supernode's canonical view always matches verifiedDB and this guard never fires.

## Changes

- `RoundObservation.L2NeedsRewind` + `checkPreconditions` maps it to `DecisionRewind`.
- `observeRound` checks each last-verified L2 head against `L2BlockRefByNumber` (a lightweight block-ref lookup — no output-root or state-proof computation); any read error backs the round off rather than advancing on unproven canonicality.
- `L2BlockRefByNumber` added to the `ChainContainer` interface (delegates to the engine controller, already used internally); test mocks updated.
- Tests: `checkPreconditions` case + end-to-end `TestInterop_ProgressAndRecord_L2FrontierReorgTriggersRewind` (verifiedDB trimmed, WAL cleared, engines untouched).

## Not covered

Live logsDB reconciliation on a `DecisionAdvance` that still slips through, `proxyd-cl` freshness/monotonicity policy, and Reth ExEx WAL consistency remain separate workstreams.

## Test plan

```
go test ./op-supernode/... -count=1
```
